hook.text: Attractive defendants receive lighter prison sentences. Their looks have nothing to do with the crime.

buildup.text: Thorndike noticed that officers who rated a soldier as tall also rated them as more intelligent.

discovery.text: The halo effect: one positive trait spills over and colors our judgment of everything else.

twist.text: It works in reverse too. One negative trait creates a 'horns effect' that taints all other judgments.

climax.text: First impressions aren't just powerful. They actively rewrite how we interpret all future information.

punchline.text: One trait rewrites the whole story.

quiz.question: What does the halo effect cause?
options: One positive trait influences judgment of unrelated traits
We judge people only on their achievements

details.summary: The halo effect occurs when a positive impression in one area influences judgment across unrelated areas. An attractive person is perceived as more intelligent and trustworthy. A company with a popular product is assumed to have great management and ethics.
details.whyItMatters: The halo effect distorts evaluations in hiring, investing, consumer choice, and social judgment. One salient positive trait colors the entire assessment, preventing accurate evaluation of independent attributes.
takeaways: A positive impression in one trait spreads to unrelated traits
Physical attractiveness is the most studied trigger of halo effects
The halo effect biases hiring, performance reviews, and consumer ratings

faq.question: How does the halo effect affect hiring?
faq.answer: Interviewers who form a positive first impression from appearance, handshake, or rapport then rate the candidate higher on competence, leadership, and intelligence. The initial glow colors the evaluation of every subsequent answer.

faq.question: Can the halo effect work in reverse?
faq.answer: Yes, the horn effect or reverse halo. A single negative impression, such as being physically unattractive or making one mistake, causes people to rate the person negatively across all dimensions, including unrelated competencies.
